references.text: Israel is called 'children of the Lord your God' – an Old Testament background for the idea of being God's children ([ref:Deut 14:1|Deuteronomy 14:1]).
Hosea prophesies that those who were not God's people shall be called 'children of the living God' – an eschatological vision of expanded sonship ([ref:Hos 2:1|Hosea 2:1]).

The preceding verse tells us he came to his own, but they did not receive him – verse 12 expresses the contrast: those who instead received him were given the right to become God's children ([ref:John 1:11|John 1:11]).
The following verse elaborates on what this sonship entails: they are born of God, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man ([ref:John 1:13|John 1:13]).
Jesus explains that whoever believes in God's only Son shall not perish – faith in his name gives eternal life, parallel to becoming God's children through faith ([ref:John 3:16-18|John 3:16-18]).
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life – faith as the condition for salvation, just as faith in John 1:12 gives the right to become God's children ([ref:John 3:36|John 3:36]).
Jesus was to die not only for the people, but also to gather into one the scattered children of God – sonship as a fruit of Christ's work ([ref:John 11:52|John 11:52]).

The purpose statement of the Gospel of John: 'that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name' – faith in the name as the source of life, parallel to John 1:12 ([ref:John 20:31|John 20:31]).

Paul describes those led by God's Spirit as God's children, and the Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are God's children – elaborating on what it means to have received the right to become God's children ([ref:Rom 8:14-16|Romans 8:14-16]).
Paul writes that all are God's children through faith in Christ Jesus – a direct parallel to John's statement about becoming God's children through faith ([ref:Gal 3:26|Galatians 3:26]).

Paul writes that God, in his love, predetermined us for adoption (υἱοθεσία) as his children through Jesus Christ – adoption as a gift from God, related to the right (ἐξουσία) to become God's children in John 1:12 ([ref:Eph 1:5|Ephesians 1:5]).
God says: 'I will be a Father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters' – a promise of sonship for those who set themselves apart and receive God ([ref:2 Cor 6:17-18|2 Corinthians 6:17-18]).

John exclaims in admiration at the great love the Father has shown us, that we should be called God's children – and we are! An elaboration on sonship from John 1:12 ([ref:1 John 3:1-2|1 John 3:1-2]).
John writes that whoever believes in the name of God's Son has eternal life – 'faith in the name' is the same expression as in John 1:12 ([ref:1 John 5:13|1 John 5:13]).
